title: Helper functions to retrieve user and solution objects
description:
# Description 

This PR addresses https://github.com/rstudio/pygradethis/issues/67 and introduces helper functions to check existence of or retrieve user objects (`py_user_object_exists()`, `py_user_object_get()`) or solution objects (`py_solution_object_exists()`, `py_solution_object_get()`). 

It also introduces functions to list the names of objects created by user code (`.py_user_object_list()`) or solution code (`py_solution_object_list()`). 

To implement `.py_user_object_list()` and `.py_solution_object_list()`, we needed a way to exclude objects that were already in the setup environment so we also introduce a `.py_envir_prep` as yet another object that's included in the checking environment for `grade_this()`. A Python helper function `get_envir_diff()` (and corresponding R wrapper of the same name) is used to find the differences of two dictionaries which in this case are the `.py_envir_prep` and `.py_envir_result` / `.py_envir_solution` to return list of variables introduced by student / solution code.

title: Fix feedback for returning `None` via `hinted_class_message()`
description:
This PR fixes feedback when user does not return anything or returns `None`. For example if we expect the code to return a DataFrame but they do an assignment `df = pd.DataFrame({'a':[1, 2, 3]})` they will get a feedback like this:

> I expected a DataFrame, but your code returned a None. Did you forget to return something?

title: Fix feedback issues
description:
This PR fixes https://github.com/rstudio/pygradethis/issues/64 and 2 other problems:

* slightly alters the case where user submits a normal dataframe when we expect one that is grouped in some way via `.groupby()`/`.pivot()` or other means. 
* fixes a problem with one of Python test files where `get_last_value()` now returns two values causing tests to fail.
* fixes feedback for cases when user code returns a `None` (either because they have a statement as the last value, or a function that returns `None`)

title: A pygradecode module
description:
# Description

This is a PR for adding support for checking code in Python.

## Changes

There are changes happening in both the `/python` and the `/r` sides.

### Python

There is a new module/package `pygradecode` that lives alongside `pygradethis` module that we've been mostly using for our grading of results. 

The `pygradecode` module will contain scripts to convert Python code to an XML representation of its AST (`ast_to_xml.py`), general xml utility functions (`xml_utils.py`), or API facing `find_<target elements>.py` scripts like `find_functions.py` that contains functions like `find_functions()`.

### R

The R side imports the `pygradecode` module/package, and exports R wrapper functions around the pure Python functions directly via `reticulate` with the naming convention `py_find_<element>()`. They are then available to use in checking code in `grade_this()`, and we can use new functions `py_fail_if_not_found()` and `py_fail_if_found()` functions to silently pass or fail.

## API:

We will split up the full scope of `pygradecode` into multiple PRs. For this current PR, we're laying the foundations and adding some crucial high level functions to use early on:

- [x] `GradeCodeFound`
- [x] find_functions()
- [x] find_arguments(), uses_argument(), args()
- [x] find_operators(), uses_operator()
- [x] `find_lambdas()` / `uses_lambdas()`
- [x] `find_attributes()`
- [x] `find_properties()`
- [x] `find_method_chains()`
- [x] pretty print format as close to `{gradecode}`
- [x] chain-able `find_*()` (this is definitely bigger work that could be a separate PR, but it's doable: we can use R piping but internal Python functions will know if the first input `code` is just a string in which case it's a new `GradeCodeFound` or if it's already a `GradeCodeFound` in which case we'd add query results to a stack)
- [x] `py_find_functions()`, `py_find_lambdas()`, `py_find_arguments()`
- [x] `py_fail_if_not_found()`, `py_fail_if_found()`
- [x] Resolve `.user_code` object
- [x] Handle Python exceptions
- [x] R wrapper unit tests

title: Functions to compare values
description:
# Description

This PR introduces generic for `identical()` and `waldo::compare_proxy()` methods so comparison functions in R like `identical()`, `gradethis::pass_if_equal()` and `gradethis::fail_if_equal()` will work. 

For context, we recently made a change in `pygradethis` that sets the class of a converted Python object to the Python class name. So using these functions will fail because of differences in class names. The first solution was to wrap these functions and make sure to `unclass()` objects before doing the comparison. But, this isn't ideal because you would need to create custom functions and change content that uses `identical()` / `pass_if_equal()` / `fail_if_equal()`. 

So, we are instead making `identical()` a generic and implementing type methods for R objects converted from Python using the `py_<type>` class name convention. Now, we can leave grading code that uses `identical()` as-is. For the gradethis functions, we implemented `waldo::compare_proxy()` in a similar way so content changes aren't needed.

TODOs:
- [x] generic for `identical()` and `identical.py_<type>` friends
- [x] waldo::compare proxy for `pass_if_equal()` / `fail_if_equal()`
- [x] tests

title: Type checks for check_*() functions + Makefile improvements
description:
# Description

This PR fixes issue #56 by checking object/expected are of the right type for each corresponding check_*() functions. 

## Added input type checking for check_*() functions

If the object/expected are not of the right type, a feedback message is returned using the `return_if_internal_problem()` mechanism where error (currently invoked by `stop("<feedback>")`) is caught and a `graded()` neutral feedback is returned with a message on console e.g.:

```
"An error occurred in the grading code: The object must be of type `DataFrame`"
```

and a feedback message on the tutorial, e.g.:

```
"Uh-oh! We can't provide feedback at this time. Don't worry, it's not your fault! There's an issue behind-the-scenes with this exercise."
```

## Makefile changes

For the Python side, a `PGT_VENV_PATH` environment variable (addresses issue #40)  is used to determine which Python/virtual environment to use. If it's not set, the default Python is used via `pipenv --py`, which could be the system Python, one set using a tool like `pyenv`, or the virtual environment you're currently in.

For the R side, the `install` target now will install to the R library specified by a `R_LIB_PATH` environment variable if supplied the `local` parameter, `make install local=true`.  

If `R_LIB_PATH` is not set, the default R Library path will be used in a variable defined in the Makefile as `R_LIB_PATH_FALLBACK`. `make install` by itself will install the path of variable `R_LIB_PATH_FALLBACK`, which is typically going to be your system R library.

I'm open to other ways of doing this (non env var approach?) or the name of the env var might be confusing because I think there is a `R_LIBS` env var.

# TODOs

- [x] add tests
- [x] give student feedback for the case of wrong object type BUT right expected type (returning a regular `problem`)

title: Handle internal errors for bad solution code
description:
This PR adds better handling of errors stemming from bad solution code and potentially other types of internal grading problems.

Closely following `tblcheck` abstraction of problems and handling internal issues, it introduces a new `pygradethis_internal_problem` class and a `problem_grade.pygradethis_internal_problem()` method to handle problems of that class. Currently, this is used for the internal error where solution code is broken. However, it could be used for validating inputs to grading functions like `py_grade_dataframe()`.

Given this setup:

````r
---
title: "Broken Python Solution Code"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
date: "2022-09-15"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(learnr)
library(gradethis)

# setup-r -----
gradethis::gradethis_setup()
learnr::tutorial_options(exercise.checker = pygradethis::py_gradethis_exercise_checker)

# setup-python -----
library(pygradethis)
```

# Check with bad solution code

Compute `1 + 1`:

```{python one, exercise = TRUE}
1 + 1
```

```{python one-solution}
1 + "1" # this will cause an error
```

```{r one-check}
gradethis::grade_this({
  pass_if_equal()
  fail()
})
```
````

We used to have this issue where we output the exception object directly:

![Screen Shot 2022-09-15 at 4 16 05 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9612286/190500293-a777958a-58c3-420f-ab64-39fe9ec77d19.png)

The change now cleans up the error message in Render output, and provides a better feedback since we return an actual `gradethis::graded()` back to `learnr`:

![Screen Shot 2022-09-15 at 4 17 46 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9612286/190500584-58e64342-69de-4f59-9c84-8a5fa871473c.png)

title: Safely initialize python session in {pygradethis}
description:
Fixes #52 (at least temporarily) by allowing pygradethis to load even if Python isn't available or the Python package isn't installed or doesn't load correctly.

When Python isn't available (`reticulate::py_available(initialize = TRUE)` returns `FALSE`) the package loads but prints an error message:

``` r
pkgload::load_all("~/work/pygradethis/R")
#> ℹ Loading pygradethis
#> Python or the Python pygradethis package were not found when {pygradethis}
#> was loaded. Please verify your pygradethis or Python installation and
#> restart your R session.
```

If reticulate can initialize Python but can't initialize functions on the R side using the pygradethis Python package, the error is downgraded to a message:

```r
pkgload::load_all("~/work/pygradethis/R")
#> ℹ Loading pygradethis
#> An error occurred while trying to connect {pygradethis} in R to the Python
#> companion package:
#> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pygradethis'
#> 
#> Detailed traceback:
#>   File "/Users/garrick/Library/R/3.6/library/reticulate/python/rpytools/loader.py", line 39, in _import_hook
#>     module = _import(
```

If the package hasn't fully initialized functions in the R namespace, calling those functions will throw an error.

```r
pygradethis_exercise_checker()
#> Error in pygradethis_exercise_checker(): Python or the Python pygradethis
#> package were not found when {pygradethis} was loaded. Please verify your
#> pygradethis or Python installation and restart your R session.

get_last_value()
#> Error in get_last_value(): Python or the Python pygradethis package were
#> not found when {pygradethis} was loaded. Please verify your pygradethis
#> or Python installation and restart your R session.
```

title: Support for better grading code
description:
# Description

This PR address issue #49 by introducing some changes to make it easier to check the results of Python exercises using `gradethis`. 

The main idea is to enable the use of `gradethis::grade_this()` such that we can write generic grading code in R for Python exercises. In order to do this, there's a new exercise checker `pygradethis::py_gradethis_exercise_checker()` that wraps `gradethis::grade_this()` which will retain raw Python environment, result, and solution but convert them to R objects `.envir_result`, `.result`, `.solution`. 

There are also checking functions like `py_check_dataframe()` that report problems similar to `tblcheck`, and grading functions like `py_grade_dataframe()` that signal a `gradethis::fail()` if there's a mismatch of expected and actual objects.

## Changes:

- a new exercise checker `pygradethis::py_gradethis_exercise_checker()` that's a shim around `gradethis::grade_this()`
- `pygradethis::py_to_r()` function that's a shim around `reticulate::py_to_r()` that will make sure we convert complex objects like `MultiIndex` and other data types in `pandas` to facilitate grading these objects
- a few `py_check_<object>()` checking functions to make it easier to find problems when comparing `DataFrame`, `Series`, and various `Index` types.
- corresponding `py_grade_<object>()` grading functions that signal a `gradethis::fail()` message to `learnr` when user result does not match expected
- Python grading objects available within the checking environment if needed:
  - `.py_envir_result`
  - `.py_result`
  - `.py_solution`
- tests for these changes

title: Use tblcheck for Python dataframe result checking
description:
This PR address issue #46 and issue #47 so we can use `tblcheck` to grade Python DataFrames (you heard that right!).

The author can now write an R `-check` chunk with `tblcheck` grading code for the purpose of grading Python DataFrames. In the R wrapper `pygradethis::exercise_checker` function, we:

- eval and check that the `.solution` is a Python DataFrame
- take the grading code, parse and evaluate it to prep a checking function
- we prep the checking environment by setting `.result` and `.solution` which are converted Python DataFrames into tibbles
- finally, we run the checking function to get a feedback

With these changes there are two extra features added to `pygradethis` on both the Python and R side:

- feat: a `get_last_value()` to get the last value of an expression from user code
- feat: a `py_to_tbl()` function to convert a Python DataFrame into a tibble making sure to flatten Index/MultiIndex

TODOs:

- [x] tests for the dataframe translations
- [x] make the change to `tblcheck` to produce the right function names for feedback messages (for grouped dataframes)

title: Better environment handling and other improvements
description:
This PR addresses issues #20 and #14 by properly passing environment objects from `{learnr}` for grading results, and renames many functions by aligning similarly to `{gradethis}`. 

To test this branch out you will need to build this [python_support branch](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr-private/tree/python_support).

## Better environment passing and automatically importing grading submodules

For issue #20, we are relying on passing in the global environment once within the `pygradethis_exercise_checker()` in Python to make available the grading modules required for the checking code to run, for e.g. `grade_result`. This means that when authors write lessons in an `learnr` rmarkdown file, they can simply call grading functions like `grade_result` as is without needing to import all submodules. Ex:

````python
```{python, py-ex-sumcheck}
grade_result(
  pass_if_equals(6, "The number 6 is correct!"),
  user_result = last_value
)
```
````

In a future PR, we can handle the case when someone does decide to import modules as namespaces like `import pygradethis as grader` in case authors want to be flexible. Also, we're not going to touch setup code stuff yet in this PR.

## Other improvements 

### Refactoring names

A lot of functions were named with a `python_` prefix or outdated `{gradethis}` function names, some of which I have renamed (see the checklist in issue #14). We may have more to rename in the future, but those are the main ones I can think of for now.

### Tests around the exercise checker

In addition, I have also added several tests around the `pygradethis_exercise_checker()` to make sure basic tests are working in terms of getting a grade back given `{learnr}` arguments. 

### Misc

To facilitate development, I have also added some `make` commands to the R side to help test and document the package.

TODOs:

- [x] change up the testing code to use `learnr` specific helper functions like `mock_exercise()` so it's aligned with how learnr processes exercise structures
- [x] add tests on chained setup chunks
- [x] add tests on global setup chunks
- [x] test out custom namespaces are respect for library dependencies (e.g. `import pandas as pd`)
- [x] isolate checking flow versus grading function tests (currently the tests we have mix the 2)
~~clean up dictionary objects to remove things that are not essential~~ (I think we can hold off on this for the main reason that we want to get things working first, and it's also easier from a maintenance POV to not have to continually keep a list of required objects)

title: New project structure
description:
This PR changes the directory structure of `pygradethis` and fixes issue #32:

1) House both Python (grading logic), and R (wrapper for `learnr`) into one repo

title: Migrating to Python 3.9 and using Poetry and pytest
description:
This PR addresses issues #24 and #25 to upgrade the Python version that's required and using frameworks to make life easier for package management and testing.

There is a slight change for the way the feedback message is constructed to make it easier to manage for now:

1. code text are formatted with backticks (e.g. `2 + 2`) which will appear better as markdown text in different contexts
2. when possible, feedback will include the outer expression in which a problematic node occurs, for e.g.:

**Student code:** `sqrt(log(2))`
**Solution code:** `sqrt(log(1))`
**Feedback:** "I expected `log(1)`, but what you wrote was interpreted as `log(2)` in `sqrt(log(2))` at line 1."

In the future, we need to test that (1) actually displays properly in `.md` docs and possibly figure out a better way to figure out the outer relevant expression when dealing with complicated, nested expressions/statements.

title: Refactor result grading using unittest
description:
# Description

This PR refactors grading of results using `unittest` assert_ methods for gradining `python_pass_if` / `python_fail_if` conditions and moves us closer to finishing up issue https://github.com/nischalshrestha/pygradethis/issues/16, by also allowing us to keep track of matched conditions.
